name: Pervez Musharraf
role: Pakistani army general and ruler (chief executive 1999-2001, president 2001-2008; 1943-2023)
summary: Musharraf took power in a 1999 coup and ruled as army chief and president until 2008. His record includes the 2002 Legal Framework Order, the November 2007 emergency, devolution with reserved seats for women, and a stated policy of minimum nuclear deterrence. At the UN he spoke for Kashmiri self-determination, a two-state outcome in Palestine and relief of poor countries' debts.

free-trade.rationale: In his 2005 Asia Society speech he credits liberalization, privatization and deregulation; at the UN he asks for open access for poor countries' goods.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: At the UN (2004) he recognised the right of Israel to exist beside a Palestinian homeland; the statement is about a Jewish state, so this is partial.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: At the UN (2001) he called for reducing, if not eliminating, the debt burden of the poor and underdeveloped countries.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: At the UN (2004) he said official development assistance can and must be increased; he stressed trade over aid as well.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: In UN speeches (2001, 2003, 2006) he defends Pakistan's nuclear deterrence at a minimum level and says Pakistan cannot accept discrimination in the nuclear field.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The 2002 LFO created a National Security Council with a role in governance, which Human Rights Watch and the Crisis Group describe as institutionalising the army's role; he held the army chief post alongside the presidency.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Human Rights Watch and Dawn record that under the November 2007 emergency he suspended the constitution, removed judges and had lawyers and opposition activists arrested in large numbers.

islam-incompatible.rationale: At the UN (2003, 2006) and in his 2002 address he rejects a clash of civilisations and says Islam teaches equality and non-discrimination.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: He speaks for minimum nuclear deterrence in South Asia within a strategic restraint regime, not for giving the weapons up (UN 2006).

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: His August 2002 Legal Framework Order restored article 58(2)(b), the presidential power to dissolve the National Assembly, as reported by Human Rights Watch and the International Crisis Group.

reserved-seats-excluded-groups.rationale: His 2001 UN speech describes devolution giving one third of seats on district governing councils to women; this is his own account of the policy, not the statute.

notes: Only a limited set of statements is answered; the rest are null. Searched themes: government (referendum, LFO, emergency, media), religion and women (Women's Protection Act 2006, blasphemy law, madrasas), world (UN speeches, Kashmir, Palestine, nuclear), economy (privatization, aid, debt). Several records were found but not used as answers because the saved sources do not state a position on a specific statement: the Women's Protection Act text, the A.Q. Khan pardon, and his madrasa reform remarks; blasphemy law positions changed between 2000 and 2004 and are unsettled. The uncertainty rule may fail: coverage of dividing lines is thin and most answers are medium confidence.
